narrative:
On September 25, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded a total of 1,152 cases heard out of 2,652 scheduled, resulting in a daily hearing rate of 43.4%. This performance remains consistent with the previous observed session on September 22, 2026 (42.6%), and shows an improvement over the 39.5% recorded on September 21. The bias gap between government and commoner cases remains narrow, with government cases achieving a 45.0% hearing rate compared to 42.8% for commoner cases.

Judge-wise performance reflects significant variance in docket management. High-volume benches like E.S. Indiresh (87.7% heard) and the C.M. Poonacha bench (up to 87.5%) showed strong clearance capabilities. Conversely, dockets managed by B.M. Shyam Prasad and M. Nagaprasanna recorded lower hearing rates, hovering between 10% and 21% for various segments of their daily lists. Several benches, such as those overseen by Jayant Banerji, reported no hearings today, indicating a divergence in focus toward administrative or chambers work.

In terms of hearing stages, Preliminary Hearings demonstrated the highest efficiency at 53.8%, followed by Orders (47.3%) and Admission stages (45.4%). Final Hearings saw 117 cases heard out of 325 scheduled (36.0%), a notable increase in absolute clearance depth compared to the 24.0% seen on September 22. Further Hearings continue to present the most significant bottleneck, with a hearing rate of just 17.8%.

Case type distribution remains dominated by Writ Petitions (WP) and Criminal Petitions (CRL.P), which together accounted for 1,595 of the total scheduled matters. While WPs maintained a 40.8% hearing rate, niche case categories like Writ Appeals (WA) and Civil Revision Petitions (CRP) showed higher relative throughput at 60.5% and 90.0%, respectively.
